text: Cattle disease recognition (ការសង្កេតជំងឺ) means noticing changes from an animal's normal condition and treating symptoms as warning signs, not a diagnosis. Important diseases to know: foot-and-mouth disease (FMD; fever, excessive salivation, mouth lesions, foot lesions, lameness -- highly contagious, separate affected animals immediately and seek help); lumpy skin disease (LSD; firm skin nodules, enlarged lymph nodes, fever, reduced production -- insects can contribute to spread, watch closely in the wet season); respiratory disease (coughing, nasal discharge, fever, rapid/difficult breathing); and reproductive disease/brucellosis (repeated abortion, infertility, retained placenta, stillbirth, weak offspring -- avoid unnecessary handling of birth materials since some reproductive diseases can affect people too). CBPP is internationally important but its Preah Vihear relevance should be confirmed via current Cambodian animal-health sources rather than assumed. During the wet season, watch muddy/crowded conditions and insect activity; during the dry season, heat stress and forage/water shortages can complicate monitoring -- distinguish stress or poor nutrition from actual infection rather than assuming every weak animal is infected. For smallholders with only a few cattle and limited vet access, the practical response is: notice abnormal animals early, separate sick animals where feasible, avoid unnecessary movement/mixing, and contact a veterinarian promptly for serious or contagious-looking disease. Never diagnose FMD, LSD, CBPP, or brucellosis from symptoms alone, and never provide treatment or medication doses as universal facts.
